title: Maximal Network Rank
summary: Given n cities and their bidirectional roads, calculate the maximal network rank by finding the highest total number of directly connected roads for any two different cities, ensuring each road is counted only once if it connects both cities.
statement: Given n cities and their bidirectional roads, calculate the maximal network rank by finding the highest total number of directly connected roads for any two different cities, ensuring each road is counted only once if it connects both cities.
constraints: 2–100 cities; roads are unique undirected pairs.
For every pair of cities, count all incident roads once, including their direct road only once.
hints: A pair’s rank is the sum of its degrees minus one when the cities are directly linked.
Build neighbor sets, then evaluate every unordered city pair.
For a<b, add both set sizes and subtract membership of b in a’s set.
Every road incident to either city appears once in a degree sum, except their shared road appears in both and needs one subtraction.
editorial: Every road incident to either city appears once in a degree sum, except their shared road appears in both and needs one subtraction.

tests.explanation: Cities zero and one have combined rank four after counting their shared road once.
Cities one and two provide the maximum combined network rank five.
